SL-000014.transcript:
Member (Hannah Roy): I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Hannah Roy, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Hannah Roy): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Hannah Roy): Yes, that's right.
Member (Hannah Roy): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you go off work?
Member (Hannah Roy): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Hannah Roy): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Hannah Roy): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Hannah Roy): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Hannah Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your claim was approved yesterday. The first payment goes out Friday, and your case manager will call you this week to talk about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Hannah Roy): So when does the first payment come?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): It's scheduled for Friday, and it includes the weeks since your waiting period ended.
Member (Hannah Roy): Who do I contact if something changes?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your case manager is Denise. I've sent you her direct line by secure message.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Hannah Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
SL-000014.narrative_summary: Hannah Roy, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a disability claim status case. Agent Priya Sandhu reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list. In the end, it was resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 4 (satisfied).

SL-000024.transcript:
Member (Lucas Patel): I want to check whether my plan covers orthodontics for my son.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Lucas Patel, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Lucas Patel): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Happy to check that for you.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Lucas Patel): Yes, that's right.
Member (Lucas Patel): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Lucas Patel): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): How old is he?
Member (Lucas Patel): Fourteen.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Lucas Patel): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Lucas Patel): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Lucas Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Orthodontics isn't part of your employer's plan. I can send you the booklet section, and your plan administrator at work can confirm whether that's changing.
Member (Lucas Patel): That's disappointing.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I understand. Some employers offer a health spending account that can be used for orthodontics.
Member (Lucas Patel): How would I check that?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): It would show under Accounts in the app. I don't see one on your certificate, but HR can confirm.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): To recap: orthodontics isn't in your employer's plan right now, and HR can tell you if that's changing.
Member (Lucas Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Chantal Chen): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Chantal Chen, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Chantal Chen): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Chantal Chen): Yes, that's right.
Member (Chantal Chen): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Chantal Chen): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Chantal Chen): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Chantal Chen): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Chantal Chen): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Chantal Chen): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Chantal Chen): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Chantal Chen): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Chantal Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Tyler Roy): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Tyler Roy, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Tyler Roy): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Tyler Roy): Yes, that's right.
Member (Tyler Roy): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Tyler Roy): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Tyler Roy): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Tyler Roy): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Tyler Roy): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Tyler Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Tyler Roy): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Tyler Roy): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Tyler Roy): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Tyler Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

SL-000682.transcript:
Member (Emma Campbell): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Emma Campbell, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Emma Campbell): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Emma Campbell): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Emma Campbell): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Emma Campbell): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Emma Campbell): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Emma Campbell): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Emma Campbell): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Emma Campbell): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Emma Campbell): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Emma Campbell): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Emma Campbell): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Emma Campbell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Agent (Jasmine Wong): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Arjun O'Brien): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.

Member (Noah Cote): Yes, that's right.
Member (Noah Cote): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Noah Cote): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Where is the money going?
Member (Noah Cote): To an RRSP at my bank. They say they're waiting on Sun Life.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?
Member (Noah Cote): I think so. They handled their side.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Have you received any statement showing the transfer as pending?
Member (Noah Cote): Only the annual statement, which still shows the balance with you.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Noah Cote): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Noah Cote): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Noah Cote): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?

Member (Owen Chen): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Owen Chen): Great, that helps.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Owen Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Leila Patel): I want to check whether my plan covers orthodontics for my son.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Leila Patel, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Patel): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Happy to check that for you.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Leila Patel): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Leila Patel): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Leila Patel): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Leila Patel): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Leila Patel): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?

Agent (Chloe Gagnon): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Leila Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Leila Patel): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Leila Patel): Great, that helps.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Leila Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Tyler Morrison): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Tyler Morrison): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.

Member (Tyler Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Tyler Morrison): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Tyler Morrison): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Tyler Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Emma O'Brien): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Emma O'Brien, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Emma O'Brien): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Emma O'Brien): Yes, that's right.
Member (Emma O'Brien): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Emma O'Brien): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Emma O'Brien): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Emma O'Brien): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Emma O'Brien): They said they billed it the same way as always.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Emma O'Brien): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Emma O'Brien): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Emma O'Brien): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Emma O'Brien): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Liam O'Brien): The pharmacy said my new prescription needs another form before you'll cover it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Liam O'Brien, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam O'Brien): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Liam O'Brien): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Liam O'Brien): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Which medication or service is the request about?
Member (Liam O'Brien): A new medication my specialist started me on last week.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Liam O'Brien): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Is your doctor's office aware a form is needed?
Member (Liam O'Brien): I told them, and they said they'd need the form itself from Sun Life.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): How much medication do you have left?
Member (Liam O'Brien): About four days. That's why I'm calling now.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): I understand. Keep the receipt for the form, and I'll note on your file how much medication you have left.
Member (Liam O'Brien): How long does the review take once it's in?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Usually two to three business days. I've asked for it to be prioritised given your supply.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: the form is in your email, your doctor completes and faxes it, and the review usually takes two to three business days.
Member (Liam O'Brien): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Noah Campbell): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Noah Campbell, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah Campbell): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Happy to check that for you.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Noah Campbell): Yes, that's right.
Member (Noah Campbell): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Noah Campbell): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Noah Campbell): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Noah Campbell): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?
Member (Noah Campbell): Yes, here in town.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Noah Campbell): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Noah Campbell): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Noah Campbell): Great, that helps.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Noah Campbell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
